reasoning: Recent Texas Senate polling over the last 45 days shows a very tight race, with multiple polls placing either Ken Paxton or James Talarico ahead by 1-4 points, which is best characterized as a slight Republican edge or statistical tie rather than a clear lead. I did not find a current statewide Texas presidential general-election poll in the last 45 days, so the race-specific current margin is based on the Senate race only. Texas's statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is R+13.

sources.name: Emerson College Polling / Nexstar Media
sources.details: Likely Texas voters were split 47% Paxton to 46% Talarico, with 5% undecided and 2% for someone else, making it a one-point Republican lead.

sources.name: Texas A&M Bush School / ReconMR (Texas Pulse poll, as reported by USA Today)
sources.details: Likely Texas voters preferred James Talarico over Ken Paxton 47% to 43%, a four-point Democratic lead.

sources.name: Texas Southern University / Barbara Jordan Public Policy Research and Survey Center (as reported by USA Today)
sources.details: Texas Southern University's likely-voter survey showed Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 45%, a two-point Democratic lead.

sources.name: Fox News poll (as reported by New York Post)
sources.details: Fox News reported Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 48% in a Texas Senate poll of registered voters, a three-point Democratic lead.

sources.name: University of Texas Texas Politics Project poll tracker
sources.details: The Texas 2026 Senate poll tracker compiled recent public polls and showed the race within a few points either way, with the latest Emerson poll at Paxton +1.
